text: The Fed has reversed course to rate hikes with rates at 3.75–4.0%, inflation is reaccelerating to 3.7–4.1%, and the VIX sits at 26.36 — this combination of tightening policy, sticky inflation, and elevated fear means the environment is hostile to growth stocks and you should be cautious about adding new risk.

IONQ is down 37% with no earnings, no free cash flow, nearly 69% off its highs, and carries EXIT signal — this is a broken speculative bet and the rising-rate environment makes unprofitable companies even harder to hold, so take the loss and move on.

Palantir's PE of 63.5 is the most expensive in your portfolio, and with the Fed actively hiking rates, sky-high valuations get punished hardest — consider trimming to lock in gains and reduce your exposure to valuation compression risk.

ServiceNow is down 47% from its high with the worst relative strength in your portfolio at -46.9, and in a rate-hiking cycle its premium valuation faces continued pressure — trim to right-size this position before further damage.

Adobe's PE of 8.5 and free cash flow yield near 11% make it the cheapest quality name in your portfolio, and its steady 10.5% revenue growth holds up well even in a tougher macro environment — this pullback is a reasonable spot to add gradually.

Google is down 19% but growing revenue at 15% with strong fundamentals behind the dip — at this lower price the risk-reward has improved, making it worth adding in small increments if you believe in the long-term earnings power.
